Jackson was against printing money. He was against having a central bank like what we have with the Federal Reserve today. Ugh... I just re-read what I wrote and I realized I totally screwed it up. Okay... let me try and correct what I said and then offer some extra clarification.

First my first sentence there is ENTIRELY wrong. In my finger happy zeal to type out my response I neglected to include the most important word of the sentence which is NOT. It should have appeared directly after the word was.

So...

Jackson was against printing money.

Should be

Jackson was not against printing money.

But, let me offer some extra context where I can see how some might think Jackson was against printing money. He was not against printing it. He understood you needed some form of banknotes backed by a precious metal like gold or silver to facilitate trade, etc. Also for the purpose of this I'm going to make one other point right away. I won't refer to it as printing money but creating money as that is what Jackson was really getting at. You could also call it credit.

What he was against was having a Central Bank that was controlled by private bankers as the Federal Reserve is today. In the early days of the United States debt was a pretty big deal. You don't see it talked about a lot in the history books but a lot of the founding fathers were pretty anti-debt as England loved to keep the colonies in a noose with debt and oppressive taxes. He helped bring down the Second Bank of the United States in the Bank War.

So why did he hate a Central Bank controlled by private hands?

Because the only way a bank makes money is through debt. Debt is created through loans. Loans can bankrupt a nation.

Part of the job of a Central Bank is to set monetary policy and one of the major ways they do that is through influencing or controlling interest rates. If they drop interest rates they in effect create money because they just dropped rates for all of the banks in the nation which then encourages businesses and people to take out loans. When loans are taken it creates additional capital (or credit) because a bank can lend out more money than it actually has. This graph does a better job of explaining it than me. With these powers the Central Bank can come to control a nations economy and thus the prosperity of its people.

I don't know if that helps but that was really what Jackson was against and I think he was right for it. I think having him on a $20 is the right thing because it serves as a reminder of what he stood for.
